newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie losing ground, risks $0.7735 floor.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie losing ground, risks $0.7735 floor.

text.p: *AUD looking vulnerable after suffering 3/4 cent correction to key $0.7775 support on largely U.S. investment bank selling
*Threat of higher US rates and risk, albiet smaller, of an Australian easing continues to depress sentiment
*Failure on upside means test of last week's $0.7735 low likely and anaylysts see scope for $0.7680 short term
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the currency was fighting a rearguard action at US$0.7774/79 after retreating from US$0.7815/20 late here Monday and a high around US$0.7895 Friday.

Traders said there was still talk of a large buy order lurking in the wings, rumoured to be related to a U.S. bid for a Victorian power station, but there had been no sign of it as yet. The mere threat was enough to make sellers cautious, however, and could help cushion the currency near term.
Resistance was now expected around US$0.7825 and US$0.7850 and the currency needed to clear the latter to break the growing bear trend.

The currency was mixed on the crosses, a slightly worrying development given the U.S. dollar had pushed ahead on both the yen and mark overnight. It slipped to 98.40/50 yen from 98.59/69 amid signs of profit-taking from Tokyo, but did nudge up to 1.3453/65 marks from 1.3414/27 as the German currency suffered on talk of a sizeable sell order from a New York bank.
Overshadowing everything was the inexorable contraction of the A$'s yield premium over its U.S. counterpart.
On the short end of the curve the spread on two-year bonds, for instance, had shrunk to just three basis points this morning from a gap of more than 60 basis points a few weeks ago.

A run of strong data in the U.S. had also raised the chance the Federal Reserve would tighten again at its May 20 meeting, in contrast with Australia where low inflation and subdued employment meant the risk was on the side of a policy easing.
Some partial price indicators due today should reinforce the benign inflation background with input prices in particular expected to be curbed by the dollar's rise in February.

Inflation data were also out from New Zealand today and showed a surprise 0.3 percent fall in Q1. The market assumed this provided scope for a monetary easing there and marked the Kiwi dollar as a result. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
